Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.name: get_code_snippet

messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The test `shouldThrowAnExceptionOnTruncatedEntries` expects an IOException to be thrown when reading a truncated tar archive. However, the current bug report states that no IOException is thrown and the TarArchiveInputStream silently finishes on unexpected EOF.

Looking at the `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()` method, it calls `getRecord()` to read each tar header block. Within `getRecord()`, it calls `readRecord()` which attempts to read a full record (block) of size `recordSize`. If fewer bytes than `recordSize` are read (indicating EOF or truncation), `readRecord()` returns null.

`getRecord()` then uses `isEOFRecord()` to determine if the record read is an EOF record or not. If it is EOF (null or zero block), it sets `hasHitEOF` true and consumes the rest of the stream padding, then returns null signaling no more entries.

Back in `getNextTarEntry()`, if `getRecord()` returns null (EOF hit), the method returns null, ending iteration over tar entries.

This means that when a truncated tar file is read and a record cannot be fully read (incomplete header), `readRecord()` returns null, `getRecord()` treats it as EOF, and `getNextTarEntry()` returns null quietly without throwing IOException. This is why the IOException expected by the test is never thrown.

Overall, the failure occurs because `TarArchiveInputStream` treats unexpected EOF (incomplete header) as normal EOF, silently ending iteration instead of throwing an exception signaling a truncated/corrupt archive.

Recent bug reports about tar parsing errors or binary null username/group issues do not directly relate to EOF handling or truncation detection, so they can be disregarded here.

The root cause lies in the logic that equates incomplete reads at record boundaries with EOF instead of error, causing truncation to go unnoticed and no exception thrown. This violates the test's expectation and the current bug report's observation.

Suggested fix approach: `readRecord()` or `getRecord()` should throw IOException instead of returning null when an incomplete record read happens, to properly signal truncated archive conditions. This will propagate to `getNextTarEntry()` preventing silent EOF completion on truncated inputs.

This explains why the test fails and the bug report observes silent termination without errors on truncated tar files.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
